patients.summary: Ballet instructor who joined in 2021 with anorexia nervosa in remission and depression on sertraline. Primary ovarian insufficiency found in 2022, a spontaneous pregnancy ending in preterm delivery at 34 weeks with growth restriction in 2024, and a stage IC1 high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma treated with surgery and carboplatin/paclitaxel in 2025-2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23 y/o woman transferring care. Teaches ballet to kids and adults at a local studio.

Hx: anorexia nervosa as a teenager, did outpatient treatment, in remission for several years. Eats regularly now, no restricting or purging, no compensatory exercise beyond teaching. Weight has been steady around where it is today and she is comfortable with it. Depression in her late teens/early 20s, on sertraline 50 mg for years with good effect, prior PCP prescribed. Takes vitamin D 2000 units daily. Periods regular, roughly monthly. Not sexually active.

Allergies: latex, sulfa drugs. She does not remember the reactions, both on her old list.
Family: mother breast cancer at 51. Maternal grandmother ovarian cancer at 47. Her sister carries a BRCA1 mutation.
Social: never smoked, no alcohol, no drugs. Lives locally.
Surgeries: none.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: thin, well appearing. HEENT normal. Thyroid normal size, no nodules. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without lanugo or calluses on the knuckles. Mood euthymic, affect full.

PHQ-9 5.

A/P
1. Major depressive disorder, stable on sertraline 50. Continue, I'll take over refills.
2. Anorexia nervosa, in remission. Weight steady, BMI on the low side but stable for her. Will track weight at visits without making a production of it; she prefers not to see the number and we'll respect that.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP today. One-time HIV and hep C screening, she agrees. Pap was done at the prior office last year per her report, will confirm with records. Flu shot in October.

Records requested. Return for a physical in about a year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: No period since the first week of December. Before that, cycles came about every 28-30 days like clockwork. Not sexually active, so pregnancy is not a worry for her. No change in eating, no weight loss, no new training load. No breast discharge, no new facial or body hair, no hot flashes she has noticed, no headaches or vision change. Mood fine.

O: Weight unchanged from August. Thyroid not enlarged. No galactorrhea on exam (she declined breast exam, fine). Skin normal.

A/P: Secondary amenorrhea, about 4 months. Her eating disorder history makes hypothalamic causes the first thought, but weight is stable and she describes no restriction. Needs a proper workup; she'd like to see gynecology and has a hard time getting to two sets of appointments, so referral placed to gyn to evaluate and do the hormone panel there. Asked her to let me know if anything changes.

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of service: 05/03/2022
Reason for referral: amenorrhea

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for sending Ms. Gutman, 24, who has now gone about five months without a period after years of regular monthly cycles. She reports no meaningful change in weight, and no nipple discharge or excess hair growth. She has not been sexually active and has had no pregnancies. Background includes anorexia nervosa, now in remission, and depression treated with sertraline 50 mg daily; she also takes vitamin D 2000 units daily. Allergic to latex and sulfa drugs. Her mother had breast cancer at 51, her maternal grandmother ovarian cancer at 47, and a sister carries a BRCA1 mutation. Never smoker, no alcohol; she teaches ballet.

On exam, blood pressure 120/78 and pulse 72. Thyroid without enlargement or nodularity. The remainder of the general and pelvic examination was normal.

Results: urine pregnancy test negative. Prolactin 18 ng/mL (ref 4-23). TSH 2.5 mIU/L (ref 0.4-4.0). FSH 85 mIU/mL, well above the follicular-phase range of 3.5-12.5.

Impression: secondary amenorrhea with a markedly elevated FSH, i.e. hypergonadotropic hypogonadism. Normal prolactin and thyroid function. This pattern points toward primary ovarian insufficiency, which I will confirm with a repeat FSH in about four weeks before we talk about treatment.

Plan: repeat FSH in 4 weeks with a follow-up visit to review. We discussed what the diagnosis would mean.

Sincerely,
Gynecology

medications.drug_text: estradiol 1 MG / norethindrone acetate 0.5 MG Oral Tablet

documents.title: Gynecology follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Date of service: 06/07/2022

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Gutman returned to review her repeat FSH, which is 78 mIU/mL, again in the menopausal range and consistent with the May value. With six months of amenorrhea and two elevated FSH levels, the diagnosis is primary ovarian insufficiency.

We spent most of the visit on what this means for her: bone and heart health, the need for hormone replacement until the usual age of menopause, and fertility, which is markedly reduced though occasional spontaneous ovulation does happen. She took it in thoughtfully.

Plan: started estradiol 1 mg / norethindrone acetate 0.5 mg, one tablet daily. Continue vitamin D. Follow up with me yearly or sooner with concerns.

Allergies: latex, sulfa.

Sincerely,
Gynecology

documents.title: Question about hormone pills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, gyn started me on hormone replacement for the ovarian insufficiency. With my mom's breast cancer, is this safe for me? Should I be worried?

documents.title: RE: Question about hormone pills
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. The breast cancer concerns people hear about come from studies of women in their 50s and 60s taking hormones after natural menopause. For a young woman whose ovaries have stopped early, the replacement is giving back roughly what your body would be making anyway, and skipping it carries real risks to your bones and heart. Your gynecologist's plan is the standard one and I agree with it. We'll keep an eye on breast screening because of your mom's history when the time comes.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 25 y/o F.

Interval: gyn diagnosed primary ovarian insufficiency in June; on estradiol/norethindrone daily since, tolerating it. Some light irregular spotting at first, settled. Mood steady on sertraline. Eating well, no relapse behaviors. Busy fall teaching schedule.

Meds: sertraline 50 daily, estradiol 1 mg/norethindrone acetate 0.5 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 units.
Allergies: latex, sulfa.

Exam: well, thin. HEENT nl. Thyroid nl. CV RRR. Lungs CTA. Abd soft. Ext warm, no edema. Skin no lesions of concern. Neuro grossly intact. Affect bright.
PHQ-9 3.

Plan
- POI: on HRT per gyn.
- MDD: in remission, continue sertraline.
- AN in remission: weight stable.
- Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids (first one), vitamin D level since she supplements.
- Pap: 2020 normal, next due 2023.
- Flu and the new bivalent COVID booster at a nurse visit next month.
RTC 6 months for a med check.

documents.body: Hi Deborah, your labs from yesterday look good. Blood counts, kidney and liver function, and cholesterol are all normal, and your vitamin D level is in the healthy range on the 2000 units, so keep taking it as you are.
